title: Handoff chorus checklist and latency rollback matrix (2026-11 draft)
body:
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a compact release-day handoff and operator choreography checklist plus a latency-first rollback matrix tailored for model-serving rollouts and config flips. It's intended for the on-call release conductor + release engineers running a staggered canary across regions.

Quick notes (notes-to-self style):
- Keep the chorus (handoff cadence) tight: 15m preflight sync, 5m per-phase signoff, 30m canary watch, decision points at 10/20/30m.
- Focus on latency regressions first; error-rate and correctness checks follow but latency impacts user experience most for our customers.
- This doc assumes telemetry signals are already instrumented and dashboards pre-pinned. If not, pause rollout and fix.

Operator roles (who sings in the chorus):
- Release conductor: Aisha (owner) — drives go/no-go, coordinates comms.
- Canary shepherd: Marcus — monitors canary instances, triggers step adjustments.
- Telemetry lead: Zoe — watches SLOs/alerts and posts annotated screenshots.
- Oncall infra: Ravi — ready to throttle, scale, or flip capacity.
- SRE buddy: oncall-sre@pagerduty (primary) — escalation for infra level incidents.

Preflight checklist (T-72h to T-15m):
- T-72h: Finalize changelog and release-notes draft attached to PR. Confirm risk assessment matrix.
- T-48h: Run smoke test deck against canary baseline, capture latency histograms.
- T-24h: Populate pre-deploy dashboard with 3 pinned panels: p50/p95/p99, request errors, CPU/GPU utilisation.
- T-4h: Validate canary infra (warmup GPUs, KV cache primed for common prefixes).
- T-30m: Notify customer-success and any customers in beta via #prod-announce.
- T-15m: Run quick synthetic that simulates 95th percentile seq lengths per route.

Rollout calendar (staggered lanes):
- Phase 0 (Canary A — internal): 00:00–00:30 UTC — 1% traffic, single region (us-west-2).
  - Watch 0–10m: p95 latency spike > +30% -> abort.
  - Watch 10–30m: if steady within +15% and error-rate < 0.5x baseline -> proceed.
- Phase 1 (Canary B — limited WA/EMEA): 00:30–01:30 UTC — 5% traffic across 2 regions.
  - Decision at 30m and 60m.
- Phase 2 (Gradual ramp): 01:30–04:30 UTC — 20% -> 50% -> 80% over 3 steps.
- Phase 3 (Full flip): After 4h stable -> 100% and monitor for 24h.

Smoke and correctness checks (to run automatically + manual):
- Automated: unit smoke tests + request/response schema validation, deterministic smoke inputs for generation storms.
- Manual: sample 20 chat sessions across model routes and confirm token-level quality heuristics (low hallucination flags).
- Sanity: embeddings similarity baseline to ensure embedding drift < 2% on canonical corpus.

Latency-first rollback matrix (ordered triggers and actions):
- Trigger A: p95 latency > baseline + 30% sustained for 5 minutes
  - Action 1: Pause new canaries and scale existing backend by +1 instance (short-term).
  - Action 2: If scaling doesn't restore p95 within 4m -> immediate rollback of canary to previous model variant and revert routing.
- Trigger B: p50/p95 diverging widely (p95/p50 ratio > 6x)
  - Action: Investigate KV cache miss rates; if miss-rate > 10% triggered by model code change -> rollback.
- Trigger C: tail latency spikes correlated with specific region (region-only)
  - Action: Strip region from rollout (isolate) and move traffic to fallback region.
- Trigger D: error-rate > baseline * 3 for 2 minutes or any client-visible 5xx surge
  - Action: Immediate canary stop and engage incident channel.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Slack update (for 0/10/30m checkpoints):
  - "[Release] Canary A | 10m check-in: p95 +8% (baseline 280ms -> 302ms), errors 0.1% (ok). Proceeding to 30m. — Aisha"
- Abort message: "[Release] Canary A aborted — p95 +38% sustained; rollback applied at 00:12 UTC. Observability notes uploaded. Eng oncall engaged."

Rollback mechanics (commands and safe order):
1) Disable new traffic to canary pool: infra route toggle -> set weight=0 for canary-target.
2) Promote previous stable variant back into rotation: route set to stable-2026-09 by id.
3) If the rollback is complex (schema changes), initiate DB/feature-flag reconcile and run post-rollback consistency checks.
4) Notify customers and CS: short incident note + ETA for fix.

Telemetry and verification after rollback:
- Re-run synthetic 10k requests across observed heavy prefixes. Confirm p95 and error-rate within baseline bands for 30 minutes.
- Save full flamegraphs and GPU profiler dumps to /artifacts/releases/2026-11/handoff-chorus.

Contingencies (unknown unknowns):
- If degradation looks like input distribution shift (sudden long prompt surge): enable prefix caching and scale KV cache nodes.
- If NP memory or OOMs appear: reduce batch size on serving runtime and re-queue canary.

Open TODOs and followups (for the next pass):
- Create a tiny synthetic suite that exercises the long-prefix and short-prefix extremes side-by-side. (Ravi)
- Add an automatic canary abort rule in ops-tier that triggers on p95 > +25% for 3m (Zoe).
- Postmortem template: standardize the anomaly annotation with chart snapshots and exact timestamps (Marcus).

Appendix: quick checklist (copy as a card)
- [ ] changelog linked and PR merged
- [ ] telemetry panels pinned (p50/p95/p99, errors, cache-miss)
- [ ] synthetic smoke run green
- [ ] GPUs warmed and caches primed
- [ ] release conductors and oncall assigned
- [ ] customer comms prepared

Endnotes: this is a working sketch. Please annotate with timestamps and add screenshots of the dashboards you consulted during the canary. The latency rollback matrix should be elevated to the runbook if we see this pattern two more times in Q4.
